tempts` |\n| `GET .../goal-runs/{runId}/sessions` | The chat sessions the run produced (summaries, not transcripts) |\n| `POST ...
/goal-runs/{runId}/cancel` | Stop a run. Idempotent — a second cancel is `200` with `alreadyCanceled: true`, not a `409` |\n\nThre
e things worth knowing before you write the client:\n\n* **Always send `Idempotency-Key` on a launch.** It spends model credits, s
o a\n retry of a dropped response must not run the goal twice. Replaying a key\n returns the original run with `deduped: true` a
nd starts no second runner —\n and consumes no quota. Omitting the header is read as a request that declined\n to identify itsel
f, and gets a fresh run every time.\n* **Check `canceled` before reporting a failure.** A stopped run carries\n `status: \"failed
\"`, because cancellation is recorded as a marker rather than\n a status of its own. `stale: true` is the third case: the runner

went silent
 and the watchdog settled the run.
* **`targetId`, not `hostId`, identifies a target.** Two environments can
 res

olve to the same host with different servers, so a run can hold two
 targets that share a `hostId`.

> [!WARNING]
>
> Launch
ing **spends**: a run fans out into `targets × iterations`\n> sessions. Two different `429`s can come back — the per-minute burst
brake\n> (retry in seconds) and your plan's daily launch cap (resets at UTC midnight).\n> Both normally carry `Retry-After`; back

off on your own when one does not.

**Swarms — insights** — what a run revealed. Read these in order of cost: the
roll-up and t

he scorecard are deterministic and free, the findings registry
aggregates them, and swarm run insights run a model.

| Endpoint
| What it does |\n| - | - |\n| `GET .../goals-overview` | Project roll-up: recent runs, goal-completion rates, repeat failures, t
rend |\n| `GET .../goal-runs/{runId}/scorecard` | One run's deterministic rubric result. No model, no spend |\n| `GET .../goal-fin
dings` | Criteria that keep failing, tracked across swarm runs |\n| `POST .../goal-findings/{findingId}/dismiss` | Hide a finding
|\n| `POST .../goal-findings/{findingId}/undismiss` | Un-hide it |\n| `GET .../swarm-runs/{swarmRunId}/insights` | Poll a swarm ru
n's generated insights. **404 = nobody asked** |\n| `POST .../swarm-runs/{swarmRunId}/insights` | Request them. `202` — scheduled,

not done |
| `DELETE .../swarm-runs/{swarmRunId}/insights` | Cancel a generation still `pending` |

Two arithmetic traps worth

naming, because both produce numbers that look
plausible and are wrong:

* **Divide by `sessionsGraded`, never by the session

total.** Three failures
 out of four graded sessions, in a run that attempted forty, is 75% — not
 7.5%.
* **`failedGradingCo

unt` is not `failCount`.** A crashed judge is not a
 regression, and folding the two together makes one look like the other.
And one modelling note: a finding's `status` is a lifecycle —\n`new | recurring | regressed | resolved`. `dismissed` is *not* one
of them.\nDismissal is the orthogonal `dismissedAt`, so a finding can be both recurring\nand dismissed, and hiding one never claim

s it stopped happening.

> [!WARNING]
>
> Requesting swarm run insights consumes **no credits** — the model cost is on
> MCPJ
am. It still counts against the `insightsPerDay` ledger, which counts\n> REQUESTS and is **shared** with eval-run and user-testing
insights, so a\n> request here takes one from there too. Poll the `GET` rather than\n> re-requesting; `force: true` deliberately

takes a second slice.
>
> Three refusals, three different meanings: a short `429` is the per-minute
> brake (wait seconds), a `
429` naming `insightsPerDay` is the daily ledger\n> (its `Retry-After`, when present, counts to UTC midnight), and a `403` means\n
> the feature is not available to your organization — waiting will never help.\n\n**User testing** (`/projects/{projectId}/environ
ments/{environmentId}/study`,\n`.../studies/...`) — publishing an environment for real visitors, reading what\nthey did, and contr

olling who can reach it. A **study** is a published
environment: one per environment, addressed by its own id once it exists.
| Endpoint | What it does |\n| - | - |\n| `PUT .../environments/{environmentId}/study` | **Publish.** Idempotent — republishing re
turns the existing study, and `created: false` says so. Project **admin** |\n| `DELETE .../environments/{environmentId}/study` | *
*Unpublish.** The link dies and live sessions end. `deleted: false` when there was nothing published |\n| `PATCH .../studies/{stud
yId}` | Rename, re-describe, or change `mode` |\n| `GET .../studies/{studyId}/sessions` | What visitors did: one row per session,
with feedback and a first-message preview |\n| `GET .../studies/{studyId}/sessions/{sessionId}` | One session's transcript, paged.
Tool payloads and blobs are dropped |\n| `PUT .../studies/{studyId}/guest-execution` | The spend dial for anonymous visitors: dai
ly credits, computer starts, concurrency |\n| `POST .../studies/{studyId}/rotate-link` | **Mint a new share link.** No body — the
new secret is minted server-side |\n| `PUT .../studies/{studyId}/members` | Invite someone (or change their role) on an `invited_o
nly` study |\n| `DELETE .../studies/{studyId}/members/{memberIdOrEmail}` | Remove someone. Their grant is revoked, ending their li

ve sessions |
| `POST .../studies/{studyId}/rebind` | Point the study at a different environment in the same project |

> [!WAR

NING]
>
> **Rotating the link does not evict anyone who already used it.** It stops the
> old URL from granting NEW access; the
grants already redeemed under it stay\n> valid. That is the single most important thing to know here, because rotation\n> is what
you reach for when a link leaks — and on its own it does not undo the\n> leak. Rotate *and* remove the members you did not intend

to have.
>
> What DOES take effect at once, ending live sessions rather than waiting for
> expiry: unpublishing, tightening `m
ode`, and removing a member. Those bump\n> the study's `accessVersion`, and a session minted under an older version\n> stops worki

ng. None of them reverse by calling the opposite — a re-invited
> member gets a new session, not their old one.
>
> Read `acces

sVersion` off the publish and rebind responses. The update and
> rotate responses do not carry it.

**User testing — what visit
ors did** — the analytics reads, and the model pass\nover them. Read these in cost order: metrics, usage and signals are\ndetermin

istic and free; the insights request runs a model.

| Endpoint | What it does |
| - | - |
| `GET .../studies/{studyId}/metrics
` | Volumes, completion and feedback rates. `?population=real\\|synthetic` splits real visitors from swarm runs |\n| `GET .../stud
ies/{studyId}/usage` | Which models, tools and servers the sessions used. **Check `scan.truncated`** before quoting a rate |\n| `G
ET .../studies/{studyId}/signals` | What the miner found in the current window — and where you get the `windowId` |\n| `GET .../st
udies/{studyId}/findings` | Every finding raised over this study, dismissed ones included |\n| `GET .../studies/{studyId}/windows/
{windowId}/insights` | One window's insights. **`404` means nobody asked**, which is not the same as `pending` |\n| `POST .../stud
ies/{studyId}/insights` | **No credits; counts against `insightsPerDay`.** `202` with the `windowId` to poll. `409` if the window
has not been mined yet |\n| `DELETE .../studies/{studyId}/insights` | Release a generation stuck `pending`. Takes `windowId` in th
e body |\n| `POST .../studies/{studyId}/findings/{findingId}/dismiss` | Dismiss a finding. Keyed on its stable id, so it stays dis

missed when insights regenerate |
| `POST .../studies/{studyId}/findings/{findingId}/undismiss` | Undo that |

The `usage` resp
onse includes an `analysis` summary: `total`, `analyzed`,\n`pending`, `running`, `failed`, `skipped`, and `deferred` describe sess
ion\ncoverage. Failure/skip reasons and `deferredUntil` explain incomplete work;\n`awaitingTaxonomy`, `unassigned`, and `staleAssi
gnments` distinguish catalog\ncoverage from extraction. `projectionPending` and `projectionFailed` describe\nthe map independently

. Reading this response never starts analysis.
